title: TAM began as a place. TAM is becoming a network.
dek: Why TAM.TV exists, and what happens to a music venue when it stops being tied to one building.
author: TAM
body: For six years TAM has been a room in Elephant & Castle where live music happened. Over that time it built something harder to see than a stage: relationships with artists and musicians, an audience, and an archive of nights that mattered to the people who were there.
The building is one part of TAM. The larger asset is the community, the content, the relationships and the cultural memory being made around it.

TAM.TV is where that continues. Every TAM Festival event now creates a set of things that last: a performance film, clips, an interview, photographs, a written profile and a permanent artist page. The live night is the raw material. TAM.TV turns it into media that can be found, shared and returned to.
TAM isn't leaving the venue. It's leaving the limitations of the venue behind.

title: How one night becomes a dozen stories
dek: The TAM loop: event, content, distribution, discovery, audience, and the next event.
author: TAM
body: An emerging artist plays TAM. That single set can become a full performance film, three to ten short clips, an interview, backstage footage, a photographer's gallery, a written profile, a radio segment and a searchable artist page.
Social platforms carry the clips. Every clip points back to TAM.TV, where the artist's page links their music, their performances and their next appearance.
Instead of event, finished, it becomes event, content, distribution, discovery, audience, data, next event.

title: Project: Dana's documentary
dek: A long-running TAM project in development. This page will collect interviews, clips and archive material as the film takes shape.
author: TAM
body: Some TAM stories are longer than a single night. Dana's documentary is one of them: a film in development that draws on TAM's people, performances and archive.
As the project develops, this page will gather the interviews, clips, archival material and articles it produces, so the story can be followed while it is being made.
